speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing agitation and noticing a yellowish discoloration of your skin and eyes. To understand what is causing these symptoms, have you been feeling excessively tired, losing your appetite, or noticing any dark urine recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behaviors and substance use, have you experienced any flu-like symptoms, muscle aches, or fever in the last few days? REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Tests, CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, HIV Antibody/Antigen, RPR, Hepatitis B Surface Antigen, and Hepatitis C Antibody.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 16.3 g/dL, Hematocrit: 47%, Leukocyte_Count: 9,750/mm3, Neutrophils: 58%, Bands: 2%, Eosinophils: 1%, Basophils: 0%, Lymphocytes: 24%, Monocytes: 2%, Platelet_Count: 365,000/mm3, Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis C with fulminant hepatic failure. The markedly elevated AST/ALT (>1000 IU/L), profound coagulopathy (INR 1.5), and severe hyperbilirubinemia (25 mg/dL) in a patient with high-risk sexual history and substance use are diagnostic of acute viral hepatitis. Given the severity of liver failure and agitation, immediate admission, antiviral therapy, and monitoring for encephalopathy are required.
